posts.author: Winshifter
posts.body: Looking at your examples, VS Weapon animations will not do what you want, the tag you have in your last image only supplants the attack motion for the motion you have selected, it doesn't change that particular motion. For example, the <Weapon Motion:guard> will make that, when you select the attack command and the character moves to attack, the motion used for animating the batler will be the guard motion from the battler's motion, not that it will show that particular file for the weapon when you select guard command, VS Weapon animations doesn't consider such things. Unless there is a plugin that specificaly handles that kind of logic that is compatible with Visustella plugins, your best bet is to basically draw the weapons directly into different files and handle a parallel common event to update that based on the equiped weapon, basically like your first image in your last post.

I purchased the plugin and now reading through the manual.
It seems like I have three options to pick from.
Option 1: SV Equip Sprite Expansion Plugin
Pro - It would allow me to customize weapon animations over each motion type.
Con - Risk compatibility issues with VisuStella plugins.
Option 2: Parallel Common Events
Pro - No risk of compatibility issues with VisuStella plugins.
Con - Would common events this large cause lag?
Option 3: VisuStella Weapon Animation plugin
Pro - Fully compatible with other VisuStella plugins.
Con - Weapon animations would be limited to attack motions only.

posts.author: Winshifter

MDR said:
Do you think a common event that toggles 12 actors with 10 weapons each is too much? Would it slow the game down?
Click to expand...
Depends on how you call and structure the common event. I think you best bet is to find a plugin that calls a common event after equiping a weapon or one that triggers after closing main menu. But, overall, a common event that only switches files every frame with a wait each frame shouldn't take that much just make sure that there is a way to skip all if there is no change, like keeping a variable with the current name of the file for the character, if it hasn't changed, do nothing, else check the current weapon and update accordingly. That way, even if checked every frame, it will do basically nothing and will have negligible impact on the framerate or the game itself.

posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body:
Hmmm, if you want to combine the actor and weapon file like that, doesn't it work if you make file Sprite_Weapon loadBitmap use a file depending on what weapon the actor is using. Then in Sprite_Actor update frame you also update the _weaponSprite frame to match. And remove the weapon update methods that would otherwise control it.
EDIT: To clarify, because the _weaponSprite is always visible (it's just set to a frame 0,0,0,0 when it's not supposed to show), so you don't have to control the visibility, only set it to correct frame in sync with your actor sprite frame change.

I disabled the VisuStella Weapon Animation plugin and installed WAY_Core and WAY_CustomOnEquipEval plugins. Then I just added the following code to each weapon. Replacing the filename with the actual name of the png file (excluding the extension). It appears to be working
<Custom On Equip Eval>
user.setBattlerImage('filename');
</Custom On Equip Eval>
<Custom On Remove Equip Eval>
user.setBattlerImage('filename');
</Custom On Remove Equip Eval>
